episode.title: A Difficult Conversation
intro: Mika hears part of Ethan and Daichi’s argument at the office. She misses Ethan’s final answer. The next day, she asks Soo-jin about it. Soo-jin says they sometimes disagree. She asks Mika not to guess from half a conversation. The subject of the argument is still unknown.
ミカは会社でイーサンとダイチの口論の一部を耳にします。イーサンの最後の返事は聞こえません。翌日、ミカはスジンに尋ねます。スジンは二人の意見が合わないこともあると言い、会話の一部だけで決め付けないよう伝えます。口論の話題はまだ分かりません。
goal: I can read a short work conversation and say what is still unknown.
短い職場の会話を読み、まだ分からないことを伝えられる。
episode.warmup: Have you ever heard only part of a conversation at work or school?
words: Mika overheard Ethan and Daichi in the meeting room.
立ち聞きした（偶然聞いた）
Daichi said, “We agreed this would remain internal.”
社内だけにする／外に出さない
Daichi asked, “Then why was I asked about it this morning?”
それについて聞かれた
Soo-jin said, “We shouldn’t make assumptions based on half a conversation.”
discussion: Why is it risky to talk about a problem when you only heard part of it?
一部しか聞いていない時に問題の話をするのは、なぜ危険ですか？
episode.followup: What is one polite question you can ask when you are not sure?

rule: Use soft questions when you are not sure.
よくわからない時は、やわらかい質問を使いましょう。
examples: 何が起きたか、確認してもいいですか？

rule: Say what you know, and say what you do not know.
わかることと、わからないことを分けて言いましょう。
examples: I heard part of it, but I’m not sure about the details.
一部は聞きましたが、詳しいことはわかりません。

situation: You talk with a coworker after you heard an argument.
口論を聞いた後で、同僚と話します。
apply.text:
Mika hears part of an argument.

Daichi says, 'We agreed this would stay inside the company.' Ethan says, 'And it has.' Daichi asks, 'Then why did someone ask me about it this morning?'

Mika does not hear Ethan's answer. Daichi leaves.

The next day, Mika asks Soo-jin if something is wrong. Soo-jin says they have had disagreements. This does not prove a serious problem. She says they should ask only if it affects their work. Mika still wonders what the argument was about.
questions: Did she hear Ethan's answer to the last question?
Do not guess from half a conversation. Ask if it affects their work.

choose: Mika (overheard / explained) the argument by accident.
Daichi wanted it to (remain internal / go public).
Mika heard only (half / all) of the conversation.
Soo-jin said, “Don’t (assume / announce) things too fast.”
choices: Did Daichi walk out at the end?
Did Mika hear the whole argument?
What did Soo-jin say about disagreements?
They do not necessarily mean something serious.
Should Mika ask them right away, according to Soo-jin?
No, not unless it affects their work.

situation: You are Mika. You talk to Soo-jin after you overheard an argument.
あなたはミカです。口論を立ち聞きした後で、スジンに話します。
task: Say what the note tells you to do. Give one fact and one thing you do not know.
メモに書かれた仕事を話しましょう。事実と分からないことを一つずつ伝えましょう。
mission.text:
Work note from Soo-jin

Your task has not changed. Use the newer financial report for your slides. Ask Daichi if you cannot find a number.

Bring your slides to room B at three this afternoon. We will check them together.

I do not know what the argument was about. Do not repeat a guess as a fact.
mission.title: Soo-jin's new work note
lines: Mika, which report should you use?
Who can help if a number is missing?
When and where will we check the slides?
Do we know what the argument was about?
What can you say without guessing?
mission.evidence: Use the newer report. Ask Daichi about missing numbers. Meet in room B at three this afternoon. The subject of the argument is unknown. Do not claim that either colleague shared the files outside the company.

topics: When is it okay to ask a question at work?
What is a polite way to ask for clarification?
What can happen when people misunderstand a message?
What kind of information should stay internal?
Why do companies keep some topics internal?
How can you avoid sharing rumors?
What helps you stay calm at work?
How do deadlines change people’s behavior?
What do you do when coworkers disagree?
trivia: In many offices, meeting rooms have glass walls, but voices can still be unclear.
多くのオフィスでは会議室がガラス張りでも、声ははっきり聞こえないことがあります。
episode.closing: Mika still does not know what the argument was about, so she decides not to assume anything.

review.manualReview: Reviewed and edited for the new friendship-only outline, simple language, explicit roles, fresh reading evidence and consistent keys.
